claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. To assess his eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more detail about your circumstances.

**Are you the parent or guardian with responsibility for Alex, and are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and I do live in the UK. Though I should mention that Alex doesn't actually live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Can you tell me why Alex isn't currently living with you? For example, is he in care, living with another family member, or in another situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mother - my ex-partner. But I do contribute financially towards his upkeep - I help out with money for his clothes, school things, that sort of thing regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I understand you're contributing financially to Alex's care, even though he lives with his mother.

**Does Alex's mother currently claim Child Benefit for him, or are you aware of whether anyone else is claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't claim Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is claiming it at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Let me ask another important question:

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, EU citizen, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, so no issues there with residency or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's useful information.

**Can you tell me about your current income or financial situation? Specifically, do you receive any benefits, and what is your approximate annual income (if you're happy to share)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm happy to share that. I work full-time and my income is fairly average - nothing particularly high. I don't receive any benefits myself. Why do you ask - does my income affect whether I can claim Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! Yes, income can be relevant to Child Benefit eligibility. There's a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income exceeds a certain threshold, which can affect your eligibility or the amount you receive.

To get a clearer picture, could you give me a bit more detail:

**What is your approximate annual income before tax? For example, is it around £20,000, £40,000, £60,000, or higher?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's around £35,000 a year before tax, so somewhere in the middle range I'd say.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful context.

**One more important question: Are you currently the person who is primarily responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upbringing? In other words, is he living with you as part of your household on a regular basis?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, as I mentioned earlier, he lives with his mother full-time. He's not part of my household - I don't have him living with me. I just contribute money towards his costs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation carefully against the Child Benefit rules:

Based on what you've told me:
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex is your 8-year-old son
- Alex lives full-time with his mother, not with you
- You contribute financially towards his care
- Your income is approximately £35,000 per year
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The key eligibility requirement for Child Benefit is that the child must be living with you as part of your household. Since Alex lives full-time with his mother and is not part of your household, you would not meet the fundamental criteria for claiming Child Benefit for him.

The person who could claim Child Benefit would typically be the person with whom Alex is living - in this case, his mother.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex in this case.

The fundamental requirement for Child Benefit is that the child must be living with you as part of your household. Since Alex lives full-time with his mother, you don't meet this core eligibility criteria, even though you're making valuable financial contributions towards his care.

If Alex's mother hasn't already done so, she would be the person who could claim Child Benefit for him. If you have any concerns about whether she should be claiming it, you might want to discuss this with her directly.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
